# Draft:Archy (dental software)

Archy (legally Archy Dental, Inc.) is an American cloud-based dental practice management software company headquartered in San Jose, California. Founded in 2021, the company develops an integrated software platform for dental practices that combines scheduling, clinical workflows, insurance processing, and payment collection in a single system.
History
Archy was founded in 2021 by Jonathan Rat, a former product manager at Uber, Meta, and SurveyMonkey, and Benjamin Kolin, a former director of engineering at Uber. The founders had previously collaborated on rebuilding Uber's payment platform before leaving to start the company. According to Rat, Archy was founded after he observed that dental software was often more than two decades old, ran on on-premises servers, and did not integrate with other enterprise software.
Archy integrated Pearl's artificial intelligence for radiograph analysis into its platform in 2024. In June 2025, the company introduced a suite of artificial intelligence features marketed as "Archy Intelligence," consisting of AI agents for insurance verification, clinical note capture, patient communication, and billing, along with a natural-language interface called "Ask Archy."
As of October 2025, Crunchbase News reported that Archy operated in 45 U.S. states, served approximately 2.5 million patients, processed more than $100 million in annual payments, and had processed over 35 million dental radiographs through its platform, with approximately 57 employees and year-over-year revenue growth of about 300%. In January 2026, the company released native iOS and Android mobile applications for its platform.
Funding
Archy raised an initial seed round of $10 million in November 2022, co-led by Bessemer Venture Partners and CRV.
In October 2024, Archy raised a $15 million Series A round led by Entrée Capital, with participation from Bessemer Venture Partners, CRV, Alven, and the 20VC Growth Fund, bringing total funding to $27 million.
In October 2025, the company raised a $20 million Series B round led by TCV, with additional participation from Bessemer Venture Partners, CRV, and Entrée Capital, as well as 25 practicing dentists as angel investors, bringing total funding to $47 million.
